scope: Reconstruction, localization and XR evidence subset; purposive first-edition scoping search, not exhaustive.

sources.citation: Mildenhall, Ben; Srinivasan, Pratul P.; Tancik, Matthew; Barron, Jonathan T.; Ramamoorthi, Ravi; Ng, Ren (2020). NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis. ECCV.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; author manuscript read
sources.reading_depth: Deep selected full text: Sections 3-6.4 and conclusion; PDF pp. 7-10, 13-14; Table 1 p.10 visually inspected.
sources.question: Can a continuous learned volume synthesize unseen views?
sources.method: Scene-specific density and directional-color MLP, differentiable volume rendering, positional encoding and hierarchical sampling.
sources.data: Synthetic objects and eight real forward-facing scenes.
sources.evaluation: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS against SRN, Neural Volumes and LLFF; component ablations.
sources.finding: Strong view synthesis; not uniformly best: real forward-facing LPIPS is 0.250 versus LLFF 0.212.
sources.limitations: Static posed-image setting; expensive original optimization; photometric scores do not validate metric road geometry.
sources.reproducibility: Public manuscript and implementation linked by authors; no reproduction performed.
sources.relevance: Foundational implicit appearance representation; separate rendering accuracy from physical validity.

sources.citation: Kerbl, Bernhard; Kopanas, Georgios; Leimkühler, Thomas; Drettakis, George (2023). 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering. ACM Transactions on Graphics 42(4).
sources.reading_depth: Deep selected full text: Sections 3-7.4, Table 1; PDF p.7 Figure 5 visually inspected.
sources.question: Can scene fitting retain image quality while rendering interactively?
sources.method: Optimize explicit anisotropic Gaussians from SfM initialization; density control and tile-based differentiable rasterization.
sources.data: Mip-NeRF360, Tanks and Temples, Deep Blending; synthetic scenes.
sources.evaluation: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, training time, FPS and memory versus Mip-NeRF360, InstantNGP and Plenoxels.
sources.finding: 30K Mip-NeRF360 result: 134 FPS and PSNR 27.21; comparator Mip-NeRF360 PSNR 27.69. Speed and quality are separate tradeoffs.
sources.limitations: Static scenes; poorly observed regions, popping and memory cost. No automatic watertight collider guarantee.
sources.reproducibility: Public implementation linked by paper; benchmark figures are reported results, not local measurements.
sources.relevance: Interactive XR appearance; requires separate geometry validation.

sources.citation: Wang, Shuzhe; Leroy, Vincent; Cabon, Yohann; Chidlovskii, Boris; Revaud, Jerome (2024). DUSt3R: Geometric 3D Vision Made Easy. CVPR, 20697-20709.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; revised author manuscript
sources.reading_depth: Deep selected full text: Section 3 method, Section 4 evaluation; PDF pp.7-8 visually checked. HTML subsection numbering differs from PDF.
sources.question: Can images yield dense geometry without supplied camera calibration?
sources.method: Transformer predicts paired pointmaps and confidences; multi-pair global alignment.
sources.data: Mixed indoor/outdoor training; evaluation includes 7Scenes, Cambridge, CO3Dv2, RealEstate10K and depth benchmarks.
sources.evaluation: Pose errors, relative pose accuracy, depth relative error/inlier ratio; compares HLoc, pose methods and MVS methods under distinct input assumptions.
sources.finding: Unifies several geometric tasks; evaluation must distinguish supplied poses and scale alignment.
sources.limitations: Multi-view depth predictions are scale ambiguous and median-aligned to ground truth. Confidence is not verified calibrated uncertainty; highway accuracy untested here.
sources.reproducibility: Public code/models: https://github.com/naver/dust3r ; licenses require separate checking.
sources.relevance: Geometry from sparse imagery, with external georeferencing and scale evidence still required.

sources.citation: Schönberger, Johannes L.; Frahm, Jan-Michael (2016). Structure-from-Motion Revisited. CVPR, 4104-4113.
sources.reading_depth: Publisher abstract/metadata only; full PDF not deeply read.
sources.question: How can incremental SfM improve general reconstruction?
sources.method: Incremental SfM pipeline; detailed modules not extracted in this edition.
sources.evaluation: Not extracted; no quantitative claim adopted.
sources.finding: Provides an open reconstruction pipeline addressing robustness, accuracy, completeness and scalability.
sources.limitations: Abstract cannot substantiate benchmark superiority; original algorithm distinct from current COLMAP releases.
sources.reproducibility: Public implementation reported by publisher; version must be pinned for experiments.
sources.relevance: Classical camera/point reconstruction baseline and prerequisite for many radiance-field workflows.

sources.citation: Campos, Carlos; Elvira, Richard; Gómez Rodríguez, Juan J.; Montiel, José M. M.; Tardós, Juan D. (2021). ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial, and Multimap SLAM. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 37(6), 1874-1890.
sources.reading_depth: Abstract, metadata and official repository checked; no full-method extraction.
sources.question: How can visual/inertial SLAM reuse multiple maps?
sources.method: Feature-based visual/inertial estimation with map merging; abstract-level description.
sources.data: EuRoC and TUM-VI named in abstract/repository.
sources.evaluation: Detailed baseline protocol not read; no numeric accuracy adopted.
sources.finding: Public system supports monocular, stereo and RGB-D configurations, including inertial variants.
sources.limitations: Published indoor/drone evidence is not a Los Angeles highway robustness guarantee.
sources.reproducibility: https://github.com/UZ-SLAMLab/ORB_SLAM3 ; public examples and GPLv3 license.
sources.relevance: Separates motion tracking and mapping from rendered appearance.

sources.citation: Brachmann, Eric; Cavallari, Tommaso; Prisacariu, Victor Adrian (2023). Accelerated Coordinate Encoding: Learning to Relocalize in Minutes using RGB and Poses. CVPR.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; author project page
sources.reading_depth: Author page method/results/dataset sections; full paper not read.
sources.question: Can scene-coordinate relocalization mapping become faster?
sources.method: Fixed feature backbone, scene-specific MLP, mixed-view feature batches and reprojection training; pose via RANSAC/PnP.
sources.data: 7Scenes, 12Scenes, Cambridge and Wayspots illustrated; Wayspots has ten outdoor scenes.
sources.evaluation: Author reports comparison with DSAC*; complete benchmark protocol not extracted.
sources.finding: Reports five-minute scene mapping and 4 MB weights in its setup.
sources.limitations: Larger scenes may need ensembles; Wayspots reference poses use SfM; not universal metric ground truth.
sources.relevance: Research behind historical Niantic relocalization; cannot identify current VPS backend solely from this paper.

sources.citation: Numan, Nels; Brostow, Gabriel; Park, Suhyun; Julier, Simon; Steed, Anthony; Van Brummelen, Jessica (2025). CoCreatAR: Enhancing Authoring of Outdoor Augmented Reality Experiences Through Asymmetric Collaboration. CHI.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; author project page
sources.reading_depth: Author page abstract, system and results overview; full paper not read.
sources.question: Can on-site/remote collaboration improve outdoor AR authoring?
sources.method: Synchronous asymmetric system sharing captures, annotations and context.
sources.data: Formative n=25 and exploratory n=32 studies reported.
sources.evaluation: Asynchronous-workflow comparator; engagement, confidence and task-load discussion. Instruments/statistical analysis not extracted.
sources.finding: Authors report engagement/confidence benefits; task-load evidence described as preliminary.
sources.limitations: Not evidence of highway inspection or traffic-safety improvement.
sources.reproducibility: System overview public; code availability not verified.
sources.relevance: XR can be evaluated as a human workflow, beyond rendering frame rate.

sources.citation: Turkulainen, Matias; Krishnan, Akshay; Aleotti, Filippo; Sayed, Mohamed; Garcia-Hernando, Guillermo; Kannala, Juho; Solin, Arno; Brostow, Gabriel; Turmukhambetov, Daniyar (2026). Cross-View Splatter: Feed-Forward View Synthesis with Georeferenced Images. CVPR, 40959-40970.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference paper; CVF proceedings verified
sources.reading_depth: Author project page method and result table; full paper not read.
sources.question: Can overhead imagery improve sparse ground-view synthesis?
sources.method: VGGT-based feed-forward Gaussians combine GPS-tagged ground photos and orthorectified imagery.
sources.data: Geolocalized ten Tanks and Temples and forty DL3DV scenes.
sources.evaluation: Two-context-view PSNR/LPIPS versus MVSplat, DepthSplat, NoPoSplat, Long-LRM, AnySplat.
sources.finding: Higher PSNR but worse LPIPS than AnySplat in displayed table; broad superiority would overstate evidence.
sources.limitations: No highway geometry/behavior validation established; author page says some release materials forthcoming.
sources.reproducibility: Code/data link present; actual artifact completeness not verified.
sources.relevance: Close prior work for aerial-ground fusion, so combining these modalities alone is not a novelty argument.

sources.citation: Tirado-Garín, Javier; Paul, Alan Savio; Chen, Shuai; Barroso-Laguna, Axel; Cavallari, Tommaso; Turmukhambetov, Daniyar; Prisacariu, Victor Adrian; Brachmann, Eric (2026). AutoCompass: Accurate Visual Localization on Public Maps by Learning from Weak Labels. ECCV; official accepted-paper listing verified.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed conference research; ECCV acceptance verified
sources.reading_depth: Author page methods and evaluation labels; full paper not read.
sources.question: Can map matching learn from noisy georeferencing?
sources.method: GPS tolerance regions and optional relative-pose supervision for neural map matching.
sources.evaluation: Recall at one-meter thresholds; OrienterNet and GPS comparisons described; numerical plots not extracted.
sources.finding: Authors report improved localization with weak labels.
sources.limitations: No full protocol/statistical audit; three-DoF map matching is not six-DoF surveyed registration.
sources.reproducibility: Project page public; complete code/model release not verified.
sources.relevance: Geospatial labels themselves may be uncertain.
